# postplan

Publish a plan, report, or artifact as a public HTML page at `https://<draft-id>.postplan.dev`.

## Steps

1. **Write one self-contained `.html` file** — Postplan takes HTML only, so convert Markdown source first. Inline `<style>` and inline classic `<script>` only; system font stacks; images from `https:` or `data:` URIs. External script URLs, external font CDNs, `<form>`, `<iframe>`, and meta-refresh are rejected by the uploader.
2. **Scrub it.** Uploads are public and unlisted-by-URL only — no API keys, tokens, internal hostnames, or private data in the markup.
3. **Upload.**
   ```bash
   npx postplan@latest upload ./plan.html --description "Short title"
   ```
   Re-running on the **same file path** publishes a new version of the same draft — `~/.postplan/drafts.json` holds the path→draft mapping that makes that automatic. `--new` forces a fresh draft; `--draft <id>` targets a specific one.
4. **Report the URL**, adding `https://postplan.dev/d/<draft-id>/raw` when the user wants the source HTML.

Done when the CLI prints a URL and it loads.

## Living pages

A draft's URL never changes as versions accumulate, so a draft is the right shape for a progress tracker, status page, or running log — share the link once, then keep re-uploading. To keep one:

- **Keep the source file at a durable path** — `~/postplan-drafts/<name>.html`, or inside the repo the work lives in. A scratch or temp path loses the file, and a lost file means a new draft and a dead link.
- **Update with a bare re-upload:** `npx postplan@latest upload <same-path>`, alone. Every flag that mints a fresh draft orphans the URL people are already holding.
- **Rebind after a move or rename** with `--draft <draft-id>` once. That rewrites the mapping permanently; later bare uploads from the new path reach the same draft.
- **Regenerate the whole page each update.** A version is a full snapshot, not a patch, so every upload carries the complete current state.

## Auth

Credentials live in `~/.postplan/credentials.json`. `npx postplan@latest whoami` confirms them. If unauthenticated, ask the user to run one of these themselves — both need a browser or a key you should not see:

```bash
npx postplan@latest auth login          # browser flow, works over SSH
npx postplan@latest auth set <api-key>  # key from https://postplan.dev/cli/auth
```

## Elsewhere

- `npx postplan@latest list` — published drafts.
- Dashboard `https://postplan.dev/dashboard/` — versions, descriptions, detected git repo links.

```bash
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become **stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your next ref interaction.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Linux hosts can install required browser libraries too
agent-browser install --with-deps

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## MCP integration

For tools that support Model Context Protocol servers, start the stdio server:

```bash
agent-browser mcp
agent-browser mcp --tools all
agent-browser mcp --tools core,network,react
```

Configure the MCP client to launch `agent-browser` with `["mcp"]`. The server defaults to MCP protocol 2025-11-25 and accepts older supported client protocol versions during initialization. The default tools profile is `core`, which keeps MCP context small for everyday browser automation. Use `--tools all` for the full typed CLI parity surface, or combine profiles with commas, such as `--tools core,network,react`. Profiles are `core`, `network`, `state`, `debug`, `tabs`, `react`, `mobile`, and `all`; the `debug` profile includes plugin registry and command.run tools. Each tool accepts typed arguments plus `extraArgs` for advanced CLI flags and exact CLI parity. Tool discovery is paginated and includes read-only/open-world annotations so modern MCP clients can load the large typed surface incrementally. Use the tool `session` argument or `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` to isolate browser sessions.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser read                         # read rendered active-tab DOM
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide  # docs-friendly fetch, prefers markdown
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --filter auth  # one matching section
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --outline  # compact page headings
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com --llms index --filter auth  # compact llms.txt discovery
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

Use `read [url]` when you need to consume documentation or other text pages rather than interact with a rendered UI. Omit the URL to read the rendered DOM of the active tab in the current browser session, including browser auth state and client-side updates. Explicit URL reads send `Accept: text/markdown`, try the same URL with `.md` appended when the first response is not markdown, walk ancestor paths toward `/` to find the nearest `llms.txt` for a matching docs link, print markdown/plain text when available, and fall back to readable text extracted from HTML without launching Chrome. Add `--filter <text>` to narrow a page to matching heading sections, `--outline` for compact headings on one page, `--llms index` for a compact nearest-ancestor `llms.txt` link list, and `--llms full` only when you explicitly need `llms-full.txt`. With `--llms` or `--require-md`, omitting the URL uses the active tab URL because those modes depend on HTTP resources. With `--llms` or `--outline`, `--filter <text>` narrows links, sections, or headings. Add `--require-md` when you specifically want to verify markdown negotiation, `--raw` when you need the response body unchanged, and `--json` when you need metadata such as `source` and `contentType`. Global safeguards such as `--allowed-domains`, `--content-boundaries`, and `--max-output` also apply to read fetches and output.

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

### When refs don't work or you don't want to snapshot

Use semantic locators:

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click --exact     # exact match only
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
agent-browser find testid "submit-btn" click
agent-browser find first ".card" click
agent-browser find nth 2 ".card" hover
```

Or a raw CSS selector:

```bash
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser fill "input[name=email]" "user@test.com"
agent-browser click "button.primary"
```

Rule of thumb: snapshot + `@eN` refs are fastest and most reliable for AI agents. `find role/text/label` is next best and doesn't require a prior snapshot. Raw CSS is a fallback when the others fail.

## Waiting (read this)

Agents fail more often from bad waits than from bad selectors. Pick the right wait for the situation:

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears
agent-browser wait 2000                    # dumb wait, milliseconds (last resort)
agent-browser wait --text "Success"        # until the text appears on the page
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"    # until URL matches pattern (glob)
agent-browser wait --load networkidle      # until network idle (post-navigation)
agent-browser wait --load domcontentloaded # until DOMContentLoaded
agent-browser wait --fn "window.myApp.ready === true"  # until JS condition
```

After any page-changing action, pick one:

- Wait for a specific element you expect to appear: `wait @ref` or `wait --text "..."`.
- Wait for URL change: `wait --url "**/new-page"`.
- Wait for network idle (catch-all for SPA navigation): `wait --load networkidle`.

Avoid bare `wait 2000` except when debugging — it makes scripts slow and flaky. Timeouts default to 25 seconds.

## Common workflows

### Log in


```bash

agent-browser plugin run captcha captcha.solve --payload '{"siteKey":"...","url":"https://example.com"}'
```

`plugin run` is for `command.run` and custom capabilities. Core capabilities and protocol request types use their dedicated command paths.

### Persist session across runs

```bash
# Derive one stable id for this agent/worktree
SESSION="$(agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix my-app)"

# Pass the same id and restore request on every command
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" --restore open https://app.example.com
```

`--restore` with no value uses the current `--session` as the persistence key. Agent skills should prefer this over hand-built state file paths. Use `--restore-save auto` by default so a failed restore does not overwrite the previous known-good state.

```bash
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" --restore --restore-check-text Dashboard open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session "$SESSION" session info --json
```

### Extract data

```bash
# Structured snapshot (best for AI reasoning over page content)
agent-browser snapshot -i --json > page.json

# Targeted extraction with refs
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser get text @e5
agent-browser get attr @e10 href

# Arbitrary shape via JavaScript
cat <<'EOF' | agent-browser eval --stdin
const rows = document.querySelectorAll("table tbody tr");
Array.from(rows).map(r => ({
  name: r.cells[0].innerText,
  price: r.cells[1].innerText,
}));
EOF
```

Prefer `eval --stdin` (heredoc) or `eval -b <base64>` for any JS with quotes or special characters. Inline `agent-browser eval "..."` works only for simple expressions.

### Screenshot

```bash
agent-browser screenshot                        # temp path, printed on stdout
agent-browser screenshot page.png               # specific path
agent-browser screenshot --full full.png        # full scroll height
agent-browser screenshot --annotate map.png     # numbered labels + legend keyed to snapshot refs
```

Headless Chromium screenshots hide native scrollbars for consistent image output. Pass `--hide-scrollbars false` when launching to keep native scrollbars visible.

`--annotate` is designed for multimodal models: each label `[N]` maps to ref `@eN`.

### Handle multiple pages via tabs

```bash
agent-browser tab                      # list open tabs (with stable tabId)
agent-browser tab new https://docs...  # open a new tab (and switch to it)
agent-browser tab t2                   # switch to tab t2
agent-browser tab close t2             # close tab t2
```

Stable `tabId`s mean `t2` points at the same tab across commands even when other tabs open or close. After switching, refs from a prior snapshot on a different tab no longer apply — re-snapshot.

### Run multiple browsers in parallel

Each `--session <name>` is an isolated browser with its own cookies, tabs, and refs. For agent skills, derive stable names with `agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix <skill>`. Useful for testing multi-user flows or parallel scraping:

```bash
agent-browser --session a open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session b open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session a fill @e1 "alice@test.com"
agent-browser --session b fill @e1 "bob@test.com"
```

`AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=myapp` sets the default session for the current shell.

### Mock network requests

```bash
agent-browser network route "**/api/users" --body '{"users":[]}'   # stub a response
agent-browser network route "**/analytics" --abort                 # block entirely
agent-browser network requests                                     # inspect what fired
agent-browser network har start                                    # record all traffic
# ... perform actions ...
agent-browser network har stop /tmp/trace.har
```

### Record a video of the workflow

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser record start demo.webm
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser record stop
```

See [references/video-recording.md](references/video-recording.md) for codec options, GIF export, and more.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a blind A/B/C... comparison set.

usage: blind.py <outdir> <label:path> [<label:path> ...]

Copies each image to <outdir>/sample-A.png, sample-B.png, ... in a shuffled order
and writes <outdir>/KEY.json mapping slot -> real label.

The judge sees only the sample-*.png files and must never open KEY.json.
"""
import json
import random
import shutil
import string
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    outdir = Path(sys.argv[1])
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    items = []
    for arg in sys.argv[2:]:
        label, _, path = arg.partition(":")
        p = Path(path)
        if not p.exists():
            print(f"missing image: {p}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        items.append((label, p))

    random.shuffle(items)

    key = {}
    slots = []
    for slot, (label, path) in zip(string.ascii_uppercase, items):
        dest = outdir / f"sample-{slot}.png"
        shutil.copyfile(path, dest)
        key[slot] = label
        slots.append(str(dest))

    (outdir / "KEY.json").write_text(json.dumps(key, indent=2))
    print(" ".join(slots))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/bin/zsh
# Screenshot the live dev site.
# usage: shoot.sh <session> <outdir> <name> <path> <width> <height> [full|fold] [dark|light]
set -e
S="$1"; OUT="$2"; NAME="$3"; P="$4"; W="${5:-1440}"; H="${6:-900}"; MODE="${7:-full}"; THEME="${8:-dark}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
URL="http://localhost:3000${P}"

agent-browser --session "$S" open >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
agent-browser --session "$S" set viewport "$W" "$H" >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" set media "$THEME" >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" navigate "$URL" >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" wait --load networkidle >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" wait 1800 >/dev/null 2>&1
# settle scroll-triggered reveals, then return to top
agent-browser --session "$S" eval "window.scrollTo(0,document.body.scrollHeight)" >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" wait 1200 >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" eval "window.scrollTo(0,0)" >/dev/null 2>&1
agent-browser --session "$S" wait 900 >/dev/null 2>&1

if [[ "$MODE" == "full" ]]; then
  agent-browser --session "$S" screenshot --full "$OUT/$NAME.png" >/dev/null 2>&1
else
  agent-browser --session "$S" screenshot "$OUT/$NAME.png" >/dev/null 2>&1
fi
echo "$OUT/$NAME.png"

Printing 'column: 686px · 53w × 7d · unit 13px' only works if the claim is literally true at every breakpoint. LEDGER's five-size scale tops out at 22px for page titles, which means nothing above the fold is memorable. Add the two-line section-heading grammar lifted from eftakher-desktop-full.png (full-value label over dimmed one-line description) and let the name / page H1 occupy a real display size. The system-purity claim ('exactly five sizes') is auditable by nobody and judged by everybody on a 5-second screenshot. - FROM BROADSHEET — INDEX NUMERALS 01–08 on Projects rows in 10–11px mono, plate-list style. Free, tabular, and native to the ledger register; it also gives the 8 image-less rows an internal rhythm that pablostanley-desktop-fold.png achieves with URLs alone. - FROM BROADSHEET — THE PULLED BLOCKQUOTE. On Post, pull quotes physically OUT of the measure into the left gutter rather than only footnotes. It is the one move that makes the persistent vertical rules load-bearing instead of decorative, and it works at ≥1280px where LEDGER already reserves that gutter. - FROM THE FIELD — THE STAT RAIL. Four hairline-separated tabular figures under the grid: LIFETIME / PEAK DAY / ACTIVE DAYS / TODAY ●live. LEDGER's ledger section is currently one number, one grid, one readout line; the rail adds real data density at zero asset cost and gives the readout's comparison bar a stated frame of reference. - FROM THE FIELD — THE LIVENESS PROOF. Today's cell renders its ramp colour plus a 1px accent ring wherever it appears, and the rail carries a live figure. This is ericsin-desktop-fold.png's '9:28 AM PDT — AUG 8, 2026' bottom-left stamp achieved with real data instead of a clock, and it is the cheapest 'this site is alive' signal available. - FROM THE FIELD — THE TYPE DOCTRINE: 'if it is data, it is mono; if it is language, it is sans.' This is a better and more defensible rule than LEDGER's 'mono everywhere except Post body.' Eight project descriptions plus a blog index set in 14px mono is real reading fatigue for zero gain; keep Geist Mono absolute for numbers, dates, URLs, labels, legend and readout, and let descriptive prose breathe. - FROM THE FIELD — THE 404 SCRAMBLE. Settling shuffled cells into their true arrangement beats LEDGER's static ember bitmap, and the two combine: scramble, then settle into a field whose lit cells spell 404. Same thirty lines, one more beat. - FROM THE FIELD — EMPTY-BLOG FOLLOW-THROUGH. Keep LEDGER's '0 posts' monument, then put a Trace/week strip beneath it labelled with real numbers. evilrabbit-desktop-full.png ships three labelled sections (Product, Branding, Physical) with literally nothing under them; restraint alone leaves holes, a motif fills them. This converts the emptiest surface on the site into a second proof surface. - FROM THE FIELD — ROW HOVER. Fade in a trailing ↗ with a small translate rather than LEDGER's 'year crossfades to github.com'. LEDGER's version destroys information (the year) to reveal information the user could already infer, and a crossfade in a tabular gutter is precisely where a jury looks for jitter. FATAL: - THE CENTERPIECE IS SMALLER THAN THE WIDGET IT MOCKS. 686px with 10px cells and 3px gaps is, to within a few pixels, the ~660px/~9px card in current/home-full.png that the direction spends four paragraphs demolishing. If a juror opens both captures side by side the rebuild's 'measuring instrument' is the same object with the border removed. Rederive from a 16–18px cell (53×16 + 52×5 = 1108px, unit 21px). The thesis sentence survives untouched. - THE FOLD PHOTOGRAPHS AS LOGANLIFFICK. At 1440 the first screen is a 20px avatar, a 17px name, a 14px lead, four 12px lowercase words, and a hairline. That is loganliffick-desktop-full.png with a heatmap below the fold — and the direction's own risk section names this as loganliffick's fatal failure without noticing it has reproduced the fold. Awwwards is judged on a thumbnail and a 20-second video before anyone measures anything. The 'exactly five type sizes' discipline must not be allowed to veto a memorable first screen. - THE LEDGER RULES ARE STRANDED. Two 1px hairlines at centre ±343px on a 1440 viewport leave ~377px of genuinely empty page outside each one. dai-desktop-fold.png's hairlines work because the margins carry content — the 'Fig. 1.' caption, the rotated micro-label, the crossing lines that terminate on the frame. Empty margins read as dead space, not as a frame. Widening the measure fixes most of it; the rest requires the gutters to carry content (year markers, footnotes, index numerals) at every breakpoint ≥1024, not only ≥1280. - THE HEATMAP APPEARS ON ONE PAGE. 'Scarcity is the point' means Blog and Projects inherit no visual identity beyond hairlines and mono — which is exactly the diagnosis of current/projects-full.png, where all eight rows carry identical weight and nothing on the page is ownable. Without the Trace graft, two of the four surfaces are indistinguishable from a default Tailwind list. - THE 8px MOBILE CELL IS BELOW TOUCH TARGET. The rotated 12×31 month matrix at 8px cells / 2px gaps is a beautiful responsive solve and an unusable tap target — 10px pitch against a 24px minimum. It needs invisible padded hit areas, or drag-to-scrub driving the readout, or the interaction is desktop-only and the direction's headline UX claim ('you can read a year with the keyboard alone') has no mobile equivalent. This must be specified before build, not discovered in QA. - DOT LEADERS WILL MOIRÉ. repeating-linear-gradient at a 6.5px pitch on a 1px channel will alias at 1.5x/2.5x DPR and shimmer at 200% browser zoom, and it competes for the same visual channel as every rule on the site. Prototype it at 1x/2x/3x and 200% zoom on day one; have a flat low-opacity fallback ready. Also do not animate scaleX on 1px rules without settling them to a non-transformed state — the direction notes this risk and then schedules scaleX on every rule on the page. - THE PERPETUAL EMBER TICK. Last three digits re-rendering every 1.4s forever is an infinite auto-updating animation with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2 territory), it reads as a fake vanity counter rather than a live estimate, and on a page whose entire argument is stillness it is the one element that never stops. Tie it to an actual data refresh cadence, cap the number of ticks, or make the liveness a ring on today's cell instead of moving digits. - THE DERIVATION IS CIRCULAR AND SHOULD BE STATED MORE HONESTLY. 'The column is 686px because the year is 686px' is true only because the cell size was picked to land there. That is fine as design — but the footer line printing the spec invites exactly the audit that exposes it. Print the relationship (53w × 7d · cell 16 · gap 5 · unit 21), not a claim of inevitability. - THREE DISPLAY-SIZE MOMENTS, ALL THE SAME MOVE. The token count, '0 posts', and '404' are all one enormous mono string in the same slot. Two of them are error/empty states a juror may never reach. ,

Chroma as an event, never as decoration. LEDGER is correct that the expanding-circle View Transition is the tacky version of this move; it is on every shadcn demo. Server-render the true value so it is correct with JS off. - FROM BROADSHEET — Per-row index numerals 01–08 on Projects, and the two-line section heading grammar (value line over dimmed line, e.g. `Work.` / `A selection of recent projects.` — lifted from eftakher-desktop-full.png). A random shuffle of real data is a small lie about the dataset and reads as noise; digits-in-cells is legible, on-system, and screenshot-able. FATAL: - THE AMBER RAMP AS SPECIFIED IS TOO HOT AND WILL READ AS A DASHBOARD. #FFC246 / #FFB020 across 371 cells on #08090A is not 'quiet chrome' — it is a crypto terminal or a warning state, and CONTEXT explicitly forbids 'dashboard-first' and 'SaaS admin UI.' Ship the bone/ivory variant the direction itself names as a fallback (top of ramp near #F2E4C8, or halve the chroma across L1–L4) and reserve saturated amber for the enumerated accent list only. Decide this in a static comp before a line of code. - THE CANVAS-OVER-HIDDEN-DOM HYBRID IS THE HIGHEST-RISK THING IN THE PLAN AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING ON THE HERO. `visibility: hidden` on the real grid while an aria-hidden canvas paints over it means two sources of truth, a hydration swap flash, a full repaint on theme change, a focus ring you have to draw and keep in sync manually, and a View Transition that will snapshot a canvas mid-frame. 371 nodes is nothing. Build the pure-DOM version first — one wrapper custom property plus color-mix() — and only move to canvas if measured INP actually demands it. - THE STAT RAIL IS THE DASHBOARD CONTEXT FORBIDS. Four figures in hairline-separated columns with a pulsing `2.1M TODAY ●` is an analytics widget, and it sits directly under the hero where a juror's second glance lands. It is also the one element that makes the heatmap read as a chart rather than a plate. Kill it, or collapse it to a single line of mono metadata beside the legend. - POST IS UNDESIGNED RELATIVE TO HOME. One sans at 17px, no second voice, and a sticky meta rail that only exists above 1200px. If a juror clicks the one published Post, the site currently drops a full grade. Graft LEDGER's route-scoped serif and give Post a real H2 treatment. - THE MOTIF DEGRADES INTO WALLPAPER ON BLOG AND PROJECTS. `INDEX ▪▪▪▪▪▪▪` — seven decorative cells next to a label — carries no information and no interaction. That is exactly the phamcodes failure mode: texture substituted for hierarchy (and phamcodes-desktop-full.png shows the noise field running straight under the body copy). Either make Trace/pulse hoverable and wired to the same readout, or cut it and keep only Trace/week in the footer. - THE SIGNATURE MOMENT IS INVISIBLE ON TOUCH. Proximity heat is the thing people record, and roughly half the traffic will never see it. Mobile needs its own arrival beat and an immediate, obvious tap-to-readout affordance, not a degraded desktop experience. Also cap the heat hard — 55% mix plus 10% scale across 371 cells is at the edge of light-show, which is the line dai stays on the right side of and this could cross. - THE FOLD HAS NO SINGLE LARGE THING. A 143px band of 17px cells plus an 84px name is compositionally elegant and thumbnail-weak next to eftakher-desktop-fold.png's ~96px hero. Either push the display size, push the field's vertical presence, or promote the lifetime number to a genuine second headline (BROADSHEET's move). One element on the fold must be unambiguously large. - VERIFY HOME AT ZERO PUBLISHED POSTS — THE LIKELY SHIP STATE. CONTEXT correctly says omit the WRITING section entirely, which leaves Home ending on four project rows and a footer. Compose and review that exact page before anything else; if it reads truncated, the fix is structural, not cosmetic. - FOUR CONCURRENT SCROLL/FRAME SYSTEMS UNDERMINE THE PERFORMANCE CLAIM. A rAF heat loop, IntersectionObserver reveals, `animation-timeline: scroll()` with a rAF fallback for reading progress, and a motion shared-layout nav indicator. Consolidate to one rAF owner and one observer, or the INP < 100ms budget is fiction. - ROUTE CHANGES MAY READ AS HARD CUTS. Skipping a page-level transition to protect LCP is defensible, but 'header pulse re-flicker plus a 420ms section reveal' has to be verified in motion — if navigation feels like a jump, add a 120ms content crossfade, which costs nothing at that duration.

  Static on Home. On Blog/Projects/Post it becomes `position: sticky; top: 0` with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` and a bottom hairline that fades in only past scrollY > 8.

ROW GRAMMAR — one row component, used by Projects, Latest, and Blog index. Two lines:
  Line 1: `grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr max-content`. Name (--step-1, --fg, 500) · dot leaders (a 1fr spacer painted with `repeating-linear-gradient(to right, currentColor 0 1px, transparent 1px 6.5px)` at --fg-dim/25%, aligned to the 13px lattice, `mask-image` fade at both ends) · year (--step--1, --fg-dim, tabular).
  Line 2: description (--step-0, --fg-muted, max-width 46em), 6px below.
  Padding 20px top / 19px bottom (39px total), 1px --rule below each row.
  This is pablostanley-desktop-fold.png's three-part row (name · inline description · right-aligned url + year) restructured into two lines so the description gets a full measure and the right column stays a clean tabular gutter, and tightened with dot leaders, which almost nobody executes properly on the web and which are the honest connective tissue of an index.

BLOG INDEX — post rows grouped by year, with the year marker living OUTSIDE the column in the left gutter (`position: sticky; top: 78px`, 12px --fg-dim, right-aligned 26px left of the rule). A real use of the frame the ledger rules create. On <1024px the markers become inline label rows.

POST — prose inset to 624px, visibly 31px inside the ledger rules on both sides. Footnotes and asides render in the left gutter at ≥1280px, 12px mono, --fg-dim, aligned to their reference's baseline.

MOBILE 390 — ledger rules hide. Column = 100% − 40px (350px). Header collapses to avatar 20px + three 11px links (≈125px of text, fits with room); theme control moves to the footer. No hamburger, ever — three items do not need a menu. Row dot leaders are dropped and the year moves into the line-2 metadata. Post prose 17px/1.7 with 20px side padding. Section gaps compress 104 → 78, 156 → 104.

The mobile heatmap is solved by rotating the axes, not by scrolling — see heatmap_role.

#### MOTION
TOKENS
  --ease-out:   cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)     /* entrances, counter */
  --ease-io:    cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)    /* theme, route */
  --ease-micro: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)        /* hover, underlines */
DURATIONS: micro 140ms · hover 200ms · entrance 420ms · counter 1100ms · theme 260ms · route out 180ms / in 240ms.

ON LOAD — THE RULES DRAW THEMSELVES. Not the generic fade-up-40px. Every horizontal hairline animates `transform: scaleX(0 → 1)` with `transform-origin: left`, 420ms, --ease-out, staggered 60ms in document order (capped at 6 stagger steps, then simultaneous). Text blocks follow their own rule by 80ms with opacity 0→1 and `translateY(6px → 0)`, 320ms. The page assembles itself like a ruled sheet being drawn — an entrance that is only possible for a design whose sole graphic element is a rule. Choreography completes at ~800ms. Implemented in pure CSS `@keyframes` + `animation-delay`, no JS.

HEATMAP ARRIVAL — cells animate `opacity: 0 → target` with `animation-delay: calc(var(--col) * 6ms)`, max 318ms, starting after the rules land. The year sweeps left→right in ~320ms. No scale, no bounce, no stagger-per-cell randomness. It reads as data arriving, not as a party trick.

THE COUNTER — on load the lifetime total counts 0 → 6,957,491,873 over 1100ms with --ease-out applied to the value (not to a transform). Tabular numerals mean the width is fixed from frame one; CLS contribution is exactly 0. Then, because CONTEXT states today's cell is a live estimate, the last three digits re-render every 1400ms in --ember at 55%. One digit column moving on an otherwise dead-still page.

HOVER — three sub-pixel-honest changes on a project row, nothing more: dot leaders go 25% → 60% opacity (200ms), the year crossfades to the repo host `github.com ↗` with a 2px y-shift (140ms, tabular so nothing reflows), and the row's bottom hairline goes --rule → --rule-strong (200ms). Nav and social underlines scale from center, 140ms, --ease-micro.

SCROLL — `IntersectionObserver`, threshold 0.15, `once: true`, replaying the same rule-draw for below-fold sections. Nothing parallaxes. Nothing pins. Nothing is scroll-jacked. The only scroll-linked element on the entire site is the Post reading-progress line: 1px tall, --ember, full viewport width, `transform: scaleX()` driven by `useScroll` on the compositor, no container, no percentage label.

THEME — `document.startViewTransition` where supported, a flat 260ms crossfade of the root, --ease-io. Explicitly NOT a circular wipe from the toggle; that is the tacky version of this move. Fallback: CSS transition on `background-color` and `color` at 260ms. A `.preload` class on `<html>` suppresses all transitions until after first paint to kill the FOUC flash.

ROUTE — `motion`'s `AnimatePresence` on `<main>` only: 180ms opacity out, 240ms opacity + 4px y in. The header, the footer, and the two vertical ledger rules never re-animate across routes. They are the site's fixed frame, and that persistence is itself the craft signal.

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — a real story, not a blanket kill switch. All rules render at `scaleX(1)` instantly. Text at opacity 1. Heatmap cells static. The counter shows its final value immediately, and the live tick continues at a 30s interval with no color pulse (the information is preserved, the motion is not). View transitions disabled. The reading-progress line still updates, because it is positional information rather than decoration.

BUDGET: rule-draw, cell arrival, hovers, and underlines are all CSS. `motion` is imported only for route transitions, the counter, and scroll progress, which keeps the JS story honest.

#### HEATMAP_ROLE
The heatmap is not a section of the site. It is the site's measuring instrument, and every other surface is cut to its dimensions.

STRUCTURE ON HOME — no card, no border, no background, no padding container. It occupies the full 686px column, bounded only by the same hairlines every other section uses. Reading top to bottom:
  Label row (12px): `AI ACTIVITY` left in --fg-dim uppercase 0.1em; `AUG 2025 — AUG 2026` right, tabular.
  26px.
  The display number, 6,957,491,873, at clamp(2.25rem, 10vw, 5.5rem), weight 300, tracking -0.035em, with `lifetime tokens` at 12px --fg-dim baseline-aligned to its right edge.
  39px.
  Month labels at 12px --fg-dim, positioned at the first column of each month — not evenly distributed, which is the detail every GitHub clone gets wrong. Weekday labels are omitted entirely; a single 1px tick at the left edge marks the Monday row.
  13px.
  The grid: one `<svg>` with 371 `<rect>`, 10px cells, 3px gaps, `rx="1"` (nearly square — squares read as ledger, 4px rounding reads as GitHub; the 1px is the tell that it is ours), `shape-rendering: crispEdges`. One paint, one DOM node, no 371 divs.
  13px.
  The readout line, described in signature_moments — the tooltip that isn't.
  Legend right-aligned in that same row: `less ▫▫▫▫▪ more` using the real 5 ramp swatches at 8px.

WHY IT IS THE CENTERPIECE AND NOT A WIDGET — it is the widest element on the site, it sits directly under the largest type on the site, it owns the only chroma on the site, and its geometry defines the column and spacing unit of every other page. current/home-full.png shows the opposite: the grid sealed inside a rounded bordered card with its own internal padding and its own legend chrome, visually bolted on and clearly copied from another product. Here, removing the heatmap would collapse the layout system, which is exactly the relationship a centerpiece should have.

MOBILE — the axes rotate rather than scroll, and this is where the direction earns real UX credit. 53 columns at 13px will never fit in 350px, and horizontal scroll on a year grid is a genuinely bad experience. Below 768px the grid re-renders as a 12-row × 31-column month matrix: 8px cells, 2px gaps (10px pitch), 31 columns = 310px, plus a 32px left label column for `JAN`–`DEC` at 10px = 342px, fitting inside the 350px mobile column with room. Height 12 × 10 = 120px. Cells beyond a month's length are simply absent, giving the block a ragged right edge that honestly reads as a calendar. Tap any cell and the same readout component updates. It is more legible than the desktop view, it reveals monthly rhythm that the 53-week view hides, and it is a better mobile heatmap than any GitHub clone currently shipping.

ELSEWHERE — the grid appears on no other page, because scarcity is the point. But its DNA is everywhere: the 686px measure, the 13px lattice, the 10px cell in the 404 bitmap, and the 8px legend swatches reused as the only non-text glyphs on the site.

DATA HONESTY — fixture fallback renders identically with a `fixture` marker in the label row at 12px --fg-dim. No fake data is ever invented to fill a grid, and no fake activity strips are added to project rows to make them look richer.

#### PER_SURFACE
HOME — 78px air · header row · rule · 104px · masthead: 44px grayscale avatar with a 1px --rule ring, 26px, then `Dhruv Sharma` at 17px/500 followed inline on the same line by ` — Design Engineer, AI-pilled.` in --fg-muted (evilrabbit-desktop-full.png's exact device: bold name, gray continuation, one line, no display heading). Below it a 14px --fg-muted lead capped at 34em: "Builds and thinks with agents as the default way of working. Writes down the judgment behind what ships." 26px, then social links as four 12px lowercase words `x  github  linkedin  email` at 13px gaps, each with a transparent 1px underline that becomes --rule-strong on hover with no layout shift. The circular icon chips in current/home-full.png are deleted — they are the single most generic element on the current page. · 104px · rule · THE LEDGER (see heatmap_role) · 104px · rule · SELECTED WORK: label row with `all projects ↗` right-aligned, then 4 rows in the standard grammar · 104px · LATEST: same grammar, dates in the right column · 156px · rule · footer: `© 2026 Dhruv Sharma` left, `x · github · linkedin · email · rss` right, plus the one-line spec `column: 686px · 53w × 7d · unit 13px` at --fg-dim · 78px air. Zero dead space.

BLOG INDEX — header · 104px · `BLOG` label at 12px uppercase · rule · 14px lead · 52px · post rows in the standard grammar, grouped by year, year markers sticky in the left gutter outside the ledger rule. Row: title at 17px, description at 14px --fg-muted, right column `2026-08-08 · 7 min` tabular.
  EMPTY (the likely first-ship state) — `0 posts` at the full display size in --fg-dim, then 14px --fg-muted: "Writing lands here. The first is in progress." and `rss ↗`. No illustration, no "coming soon" badge, no fake sample essays. The absence is rendered at monument scale, which converts the weakest moment on the site into one of its three boldest.

POST — sticky header with a 1px ember progress line at its bottom edge · `← blog` at 12px · title at 22px mono 500 (deliberately small, and more confident for it) · 12px metadata line `2026-08-08 · 7 min · design, agents`, tabular · rule · 52px · body in Newsreader 19px/1.72 at 624px, --fg at 92%, paragraph spacing 26px. H2 is 12px Geist Mono 500 uppercase 0.1em --fg-dim with a hairline above spanning the measure, 52px above / 26px below — a heading smaller than its own body text, distinguished by weight, color, casing, and rule alone. Inline links: 1px --rule-strong underline at 3px offset, → --ember on hover in 140ms. Blockquote: no quote marks, no italics, indented 26px behind a 1px ember rule at 30%. Code: Geist Mono 13px on --bg-raise, hairline top and bottom only, full-bleed to the measure, no rounded corners, sugar-high tokens mapped to --fg / --fg-muted / --fg-dim / --ember with no rainbow. Footnotes in the left gutter at ≥1280px. Footer of the post: prev/next in the standard row grammar.

PROJECTS — header · 104px · `PROJECTS / 8` with the count tabular · rule · 14px lead · 52px · all 8 rows in the standard grammar with year in the right column, swapping to `github.com ↗` on hover. Compared with current/projects-full.png, which stacks name and description with hairlines and shows neither year nor destination and offers no interaction, this adds a tabular right gutter, dot leaders, and a hover that tells you where the link goes before you click it. No fake activity strips, no tag chips, no thumbnails, no detail pages — CONTEXT forbids them and the direction does not need them.

404 — `404` at the display size in --fg-dim, then `this page is not in the ledger.` at 14px, then `← home`. Below, a 53×7 grid at full --measure where every cell is L0 except those spelling 404 in a 5×7 bitmap, lit in --ember. Static under reduced-motion, sweeps in left→right otherwise. It costs about twenty lines, speaks the site's own language, and is the thing people post.

# LEDGER — One Year Wide

The frozen design contract for the portfolio rebuild. Every builder reads this file before touching
code and may not contradict it. Changes to this file require a new judge round.

Winner of the Wave-0 judge panel (LEDGER 2 votes, THE FIELD 1). This document is the winning concept
with every judge-mandated graft merged in and every judge-named fatal flaw already fixed. Where this
file disagrees with the original concept text, **this file wins** — the deltas are marked `§FIX-n`
and `§GRAFT-n` so they are auditable.

---

## 0. Thesis

The site is one continuous ruled ledger, and its column width is derived from the AI Activity year
grid itself. 53 cells × 16px + 52 gaps × 4px = **1056px**. Every rule, row, and footer on every page
is exactly 1056px wide — the page is literally one year wide. One spacing unit is one cell pitch:
**20px**. One graphic primitive: a **1px rule**.

Restraint here is not taste, it is a measurement system. The one real data object on the site is the
ruler everything else is cut to. Remove the heatmap and the layout system collapses — which is
exactly the relationship a centerpiece should have to its page.

**Differentiation clause (`§FIX-12`).** dai.is-a.dev is the nearest neighbour in the reference set
(mono, dark, hairlines, technical framing). Ours must be unmistakably not-that **in the first
frame**, by three visible means: (a) the fold is dominated by one enormous **serif** numeral, a
letterform dai never uses; (b) the vertical hairlines sit at the **viewport margins**, framing the
whole page rather than boxing a card; (c) the page is centered on **data**, not on a profile card.
If a blind judge can say "this looks like dai", the piece has failed regardless of other scores.

---

## 1. Measurement system

Everything derives from one heatmap cell.

```
--cell:  16px          /* one day */
--gap:   4px           /* between days */
--unit:  20px          /* cell pitch — the ONLY spacing atom */
--field: 1056px        /* 53*16 + 52*4 — the year, and the page width */
--prose: 640px         /* 32 * unit — Post body measure */
--gutter: 208px        /* (field - prose) / 2 — carries year markers, footnotes, asides */
```

`§FIX-2` — the original 686px measure was rejected: it made the centerpiece the same physical size
as the GitHub widget it mocks, and left the vertical rules hugging a narrow box. The field is now
1056px, the rules move out to the **viewport margins**, and the gutters carry real content.

**Vertical rhythm.** Every vertical value is a multiple of 20. No eyeballed numbers, ever.

```
20 tight · 40 block · 60 group · 80 major · 120 page air · 160 section · 240 pre-footer
```

**Fluid cell formula** (`§GRAFT-9`) — the grid never hardcodes 16px, it derives it, so the year
always fits its container exactly:

```css
--gap: 4px;
.cell { width: calc((100% - 52 * var(--gap)) / 53); aspect-ratio: 1; }
```

**The ledger rules.** Two 1px vertical hairlines in `--rule`, fixed to the document, running the full
document height, positioned at the left and right edges of `--field`. They are the only element that
persists unchanged across route transitions. Visible at ≥1280px. Between 1056px and 1280px they are
hidden. Below 1056px the layout goes fluid.

**Breakpoints.** 390 (mobile) · 768 (tablet) · 1056 (field locks) · 1280 (rules + gutters appear) ·
1440 (reference) · 2560 (field stays 1056, air grows only).

---

## 2. Typography

**Doctrine (`§FIX-3`): if it is data, it is mono. If it is language, it is sans. If it is display or
long-form, it is serif.** All-mono body copy reads as "console", which CONTEXT lists as an
anti-pattern. Three roles, two font payloads (Geist Sans + Geist Mono ship as one package).

| Role | Family | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Data / chrome | **Geist Mono** | numbers, dates, years, counts, labels, nav, metadata, code, readout, legend, index numerals |
| Language | **Geist Sans** | intro lead, project descriptions, post descriptions, empty-state copy, buttons, UI text |
| Display / prose | **Newsreader** | the lifetime token count, the three display moments, Post body copy |

`§GRAFT-6` — Newsreader at display scale for the lifetime token count is mandatory. It is the single
loudest differentiator against every mono-dark reference site. Newsreader loads on Home and Post
only, `display: swap`, `adjustFontFallback`, latin subset, weights 400/500 + 400 italic. Geist Mono
and Geist Sans are preloaded and self-hosted.

**Scale — six steps** (`§FIX-11`: the original five had a 4× cliff to display that read as unstyled;
`--step-3` is the mid-tier that makes it a system).

```
--step--1  0.75rem   12px   labels, legend, footer, readout, metadata, nav, dates, index numerals
--step-0   0.875rem  14px   body, descriptions, lead
--step-1   1.0625rem 17px   project names, post titles, name in masthead
--step-2   1.375rem  22px   page titles, Post H1
--step-3   2.125rem  34px   section value lines, blog empty-state second line, prev/next
--display  clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7rem)   exactly three places sitewide
```

`--display` is used in **exactly three** places: the lifetime token count (Home), `0 posts` (empty
Blog), `404`. Nowhere else, ever.

**Tracking.** display −0.03em · step-3 −0.02em · step-2 −0.015em · step-1 −0.01em · step-0 0 ·
step−1 uppercase labels +0.1em · step−1 lowercase meta +0.02em.

**Line height.** display 0.92 · step-3 1.1 · step-2 1.25 · step-1 1.35 · step-0 1.6 · step−1 1.4 ·
Newsreader prose 1.72.

**Weights.** Mono 400/500 only, never 600+. Sans 400/500. Newsreader 400 body, 500 strong, 300 for
the display numeral.

**Casing.** Uppercase is reserved for `--step--1` section labels only (`AI ACTIVITY`, `SELECTED
WORK`, `PROJECTS`, `BLOG`), always +0.1em, always `--fg-dim`. Nav and social links lowercase. Names
and titles sentence case. Nothing else is ever uppercased.

**Numerals.** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set globally on `html`, not opt-in. Every
number on this site sits in a column that never reflows.

**Measure caps.** Sans paragraphs cap at `38em`. Prose caps at `--prose` (640px).

---

## 3. Color

Dark is primary and the default. Light is **warm newsprint**, not an inversion — identical geometry,
different substrate (`§GRAFT-11`).

### Dark
```
--bg          oklch(0.145 0.004 264)   ≈ #0b0b0d   near-black, a hair cool, never #000
--bg-raise    oklch(0.185 0.005 264)   ≈ #131315   code blocks, row hover wash
--fg          oklch(0.985 0 0)         ≈ #fafafa
--fg-muted    oklch(0.700 0.005 264)   ≈ #a1a1a6
--fg-dim      oklch(0.580 0.006 264)   ≈ #7c7c81
--rule        oklch(1 0 0 / 0.09)
--rule-strong oklch(1 0 0 / 0.16)
--ember       oklch(0.800 0.155 62)    ≈ #ff9d4d
```

### Light — warm newsprint
```
--bg          oklch(0.985 0.002 90)    ≈ #fbfaf9   paper, never #fff
--bg-raise    oklch(0.965 0.003 90)    ≈ #f3f1ee
--fg          oklch(0.220 0.006 264)   ≈ #1c1c1f
--fg-muted    oklch(0.480 0.006 264)   ≈ #67676c
--fg-dim      oklch(0.560 0.006 264)   ≈ #7a7a80
--rule        oklch(0.22 0.006 264 / 0.14)
--rule-strong oklch(0.22 0.006 264 / 0.24)
--ember       oklch(0.600 0.170 48)    ≈ #c85a15
```

### Heatmap ramp (`§FIX-5`)
A zero-chroma ramp reads as grey mush. **L0–L2 stay neutral; ember enters at L3–L4.** In light, the
ramp inverts — intensity *darkens* the paper (`§GRAFT-11`).

```
dark   L0 oklch(1 0 0 / 0.055) · L1 /0.14 · L2 /0.30
       L3 oklch(0.72 0.09 62) · L4 oklch(0.82 0.155 62)
light  L0 oklch(0.22 0.006 264 / 0.06) · L1 /0.16 · L2 /0.34
       L3 oklch(0.62 0.11 50) · L4 oklch(0.52 0.17 45)
```

### Contrast
Measured, both themes pass: dark fg 18.9:1 · fg-muted 8.3:1 · fg-dim 5.1:1 · ember 9.4:1. Light fg
15.7:1 · fg-muted 5.9:1 · fg-dim 4.7:1 · ember 4.9:1. `--fg-dim` is never used below 12px.

Ramp L1/L2 are below AA **by design** and are therefore never the sole carrier of meaning: the grid
carries per-cell accessible names, the readout line carries the exact value, and the legend is
labeled.

### Accent doctrine
`--ember` appears in an enumerated set of places and never as a fill taller than 1px, except the
heatmap L3/L4 cells:

1. heatmap L3 / L4 cells
2. the hovered/focused cell's 1px ring + the readout's comparison bar
3. the active nav item's 1px underline
4. inline link hover in Post prose
5. the 1px reading-progress line in the Post header
6. the 404 bitmap cells
7. the liveness ring on today's cell

Chroma is an event, not a decoration. Adding an eighth use requires editing this list.

`color-scheme` is set per theme so scrollbars and browser UI follow. `next-themes`,
`attribute="class"`, `defaultTheme="dark"`, `enableSystem={false}`, manual override persisted.

---

## 4. Layout

### Home — the fold must have an event (`§FIX-1`)
The original layout buried the number below the fold. **The lifetime token count and the full year
grid must both be completely visible above 900px at a 1440×900 viewport**, and the numeral is
unambiguously the largest thing on the page. This is a hard, screenshot-verifiable acceptance test.

```
 40  air
 24  header pill (floating, see §5)
 60
     masthead — one line: 40px grayscale avatar · "Dhruv Sharma" 17/500 · " — Design Engineer,
     AI-pilled." in --fg-muted. Below: 14px sans lead, cap 38em. Below: social words.
 60
  1  rule
 20
     AI ACTIVITY label row  (label left · "AUG 2025 — AUG 2026" right, tabular)
 20
     THE NUMBER — Newsreader 300, --display, tabular. "lifetime tokens" 12px --fg-dim,
     baseline-aligned to its right edge.
 20
     month labels (12px, positioned at each month's first column — never evenly distributed)
 20
     the grid — 7 rows × 20px pitch = 148px
 20
     readout line + legend
 ─── everything above this line fits inside 900px ───
 80
  1  rule
     SELECTED WORK   (two-line heading, 4 rows)
120
     LATEST          (two-line heading, rows; section omitted entirely when 0 posts)
160
     week strip (§GRAFT-1) · 1px rule · footer
 40  air
```

Zero dead space. The current site has ~900px of literally empty page between the heatmap card and
the footer; that is the failure this layout exists to correct.

### Two-line section heading grammar (`§GRAFT-3`)
Every section heading is two lines, borrowed from eftakher.me:

```
SELECTED WORK                                    ← 12px mono uppercase --fg-dim, +0.1em
Eight things worth keeping.                      ← 34px (--step-3) sans/serif, --fg
```

Line 1 is the label, line 2 is the value. The right end of line 1 carries the section's one
affordance (`all projects ↗`) at 12px.

### Row grammar
One row component, used by Projects, Latest, and Blog index.

```
Line 1:  grid-template-columns: max-content max-content 1fr max-content
         [index]  [name]  [leader]  [year]
Line 2:  description — 14px sans, --fg-muted, max-width 38em, 8px below
Padding: 20px top / 20px bottom · 1px --rule below each row
```

- **Index numerals** (`§GRAFT-2`) — `01`–`08` on Projects, 12px mono `--fg-dim`, 20px before the
  name. Blog rows use the date in that slot instead. Latest omits the index.
- **Leader** (`§FIX-7`) — **ships as a flat 1px hairline at 18% `currentColor`.** Dot leaders are an
  *enhancement only*, and may only be enabled after a builder has visually verified them at DPR 1,
  1.5, 2, and 2.5 and at 200% browser zoom with zero moiré. If any of those five checks shows
  banding, the flat hairline is final. Do not ship leaders on the strength of a 2× screenshot alone.
- Hover: leader 18% → 45% (200ms), year crossfades to `github.com ↗` with a 2px y-shift (140ms,
  tabular so nothing reflows), row hairline `--rule` → `--rule-strong` (200ms).

### Blog index
Post rows grouped by year, with the year marker living **outside** the field in the left gutter
(`position: sticky; top: 60px`, 12px `--fg-dim`, right-aligned 20px left of the rule). This is the
gutters carrying content, which is what justifies the 1056px field. Below 1280px the markers become
inline label rows.

### Post
Prose inset to `--prose` (640px), visibly 208px inside the ledger rules on both sides. Footnotes and
asides render in the left gutter at ≥1280px, 12px mono `--fg-dim`, aligned to their reference's
baseline. **Pulled blockquotes are set into the left gutter** (`§GRAFT-5`) at ≥1280px, 17px
Newsreader italic `--fg-muted`, no quote marks; below 1280px they fall back to the inline treatment
(indented 20px behind a 1px ember rule at 30%).

### The stat line (`§FIX-8`)
No stat rail. Four hairline-separated columns read as a dashboard, which CONTEXT forbids. Any
supporting metrics collapse to **one compact line of 12px mono metadata** with `·` separators.

### Mobile 390
Ledger rules hide. Field = `100% − 40px`. Header pill stays (it is the only floating element and it
is what makes the site feel like an app on a phone), collapsing to avatar + three 11px links; the
theme control moves into the pill's overflow only if width demands it, otherwise stays. **No
hamburger, ever** — three items do not need a menu. Row leaders drop, the year moves into line 2.
Post prose 17px/1.7 with 20px side padding. Section gaps compress 120 → 80, 160 → 120.

---

## 5. Header — keep the pill, de-genericize it (`§GRAFT-4`)

CONTEXT mandates a floating pill header with avatar + nav + quiet theme control. The pill stays. It
stops being generic by carrying the site's own motif:

```
[ avatar 20px ] [ ▪▪▫▪▪▫▫ ]  home  blog  projects   dark ⁄ light
                 └─ 7-day pulse: the last 7 heatmap cells at 6px, real data,
                    same ramp, tooltip-free, aria-hidden (decorative echo)
```

  shadow. Floating, `position: fixed`, centered, 20px from top.

  craft signal.

---

## 6. The heatmap — the site's measuring instrument

Not a section. Not a card. No border, no background, no padding container. It occupies the full
`--field`, bounded only by the same hairlines every other section uses.

**Structure.** Label row → the number → month labels → grid → readout + legend. Full spacing in §4.

**Markup.** One `<svg>` containing 371 `<rect>`, `rx="1"` (nearly square — squares read as ledger,
4px rounding reads as GitHub; the 1px is the tell that it is ours), `shape-rendering: crispEdges`.
One paint, one node, not 371 divs. Table semantics via `role="grid"` / `role="row"` /
`role="gridcell"` with a per-cell accessible name (`"14 August 2026 — 21.4M tokens"`).

**SSR contract (`§GRAFT-7`).** The DOM grid is the source of truth. The **correct final value must be
present in the server-rendered HTML before hydration** — no `0`, no skeleton, no client-only fetch.
Verify with `curl localhost:3000 | grep` for the real total. Hydration must not change any rendered
number; a mismatch is a build failure, not a warning.

**Readout — the tooltip that isn't.** A fixed line below the grid, always present, never floating,
never occluding. Default state shows the year summary. On hover/focus of a cell it shows:

```
14 Aug 2026  ·  21,412,880 tokens  ·  p87  ·  ▌▌▌▌▌▌▌▌▌░░  vs. year median
```

The `p87` percentile token is required (`§GRAFT-8`). Because the line is fixed-height and tabular,
nothing moves when it updates.

**Keyboard.** Roving `tabindex` across cells. `←/→` day, `↑/↓` week, `Home`/`End` first/last day of
the visible year, **`PageUp`/`PageDown` = previous/next month** (`§GRAFT-8`). The readout is an
`aria-live="polite"` region.

**Liveness (`§FIX-6`).** The original perpetual 1.4s ember digit tick violates WCAG 2.2.2 (moving
content that cannot be paused). Replaced: liveness is a 1px `--ember` **ring on today's cell**, which
pulses **exactly twice on load** and then holds static. Digits re-render **only when data actually
refreshes** (on revalidate), never on a decorative timer. Nothing on this site animates forever.

**Mobile (< 768px).** The axes **rotate** rather than scroll — horizontal scroll on a year grid is a
genuinely bad experience. The grid re-renders as a 12-row × 31-column month matrix, 8px cells, 2px
gaps, plus a 32px `JAN`–`DEC` label column. Cells beyond a month's length are absent, giving a ragged
right edge that honestly reads as a calendar. It reveals monthly rhythm the 53-week view hides.

**Touch targets (`§FIX-9`).** 8px cells are far below the 24×24 minimum. Each cell gets a transparent
`::after` hit area expanding it to ≥24×24 (overlapping neighbours is acceptable — nearest-center
wins), **plus** drag-to-scrub: dragging across the matrix updates the readout continuously without
requiring precise taps. Scrub is the primary mobile interaction; tap is the fallback.

**Recurrence (`§GRAFT-1`).** `§FIX-4`: a heatmap on one page only leaves Blog and Projects
identity-less. Recurrence overrules the scarcity doctrine. The motif appears in three grades:

| Grade | Where | Form |
|---|---|---|
| Full | Home | 53×7 year grid, interactive |
| Trace | every page, directly above the footer rule | 52-cell single-week strip, 8px cells, real data, non-interactive, `aria-hidden` |
| Pulse | every page, inside the header pill | 7-cell strip, 6px cells, real data, `aria-hidden` |

**Data honesty.** Fixture fallback renders identically with a `fixture` marker in the label row at
12px `--fg-dim`. No fake data is ever invented to fill a grid, and no fake activity strips are added
to project rows to make them look richer.

---

## 7. Motion

```
--ease-out   cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)     entrances, counter
--ease-io    cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)    theme
--ease-micro cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)        hover, underlines
```

Durations: micro 140ms · hover 200ms · entrance 420ms · counter 900ms · theme 260ms · route 240ms.

**On load — the rules draw themselves.** Not a fade-up. Every horizontal hairline animates
`transform: scaleX(0 → 1)` from `transform-origin: left`, 420ms, `--ease-out`, staggered 60ms in
document order (capped at 6 steps, then simultaneous). Text follows its own rule by 80ms with opacity
0→1 and `translateY(6px → 0)`, 320ms. The page assembles itself like a ruled sheet being drawn — an
entrance only possible for a design whose sole graphic element is a rule. Completes at ~800ms. Pure
CSS `@keyframes` + `animation-delay`, no JS.

**Heatmap arrival.** Cells fade `opacity: 0 → target` with `animation-delay: calc(var(--col) * 6ms)`,
max 318ms, after the rules land. The year sweeps left→right in ~320ms. No scale, no bounce, no
per-cell randomness. Data arriving, not a party trick.

**The counter (`§GRAFT-12`).** It does **not** roll from 0 — that is the tutorial version. It
**settles**: renders `6.90B` immediately (server-rendered, real), then over ~900ms with `--ease-out`
resolves into the exact `6,957,491,873`, digits gaining precision from the right. Tabular numerals
fix the width from frame one; CLS contribution is exactly 0.

**Scroll.** `IntersectionObserver`, threshold 0.15, `once: true`, replaying the rule-draw for
below-fold sections. **The observer must also fire for elements already in view on mount** — the
current site's bug is sections left permanently blank. Nothing parallaxes. Nothing pins. Nothing is
scroll-jacked. The only scroll-linked element on the site is the Post reading-progress line: 1px,
`--ember`, viewport-wide, `transform: scaleX()` on the compositor, no percentage label.

**Theme.** `document.startViewTransition` where supported: a flat 260ms crossfade of the root,
`--ease-io`. Explicitly **not** a circular wipe from the toggle — that is the tacky version. Fallback
is a 260ms CSS transition on `background-color` / `color`. A `.preload` class on `<html>` suppresses
all transitions until after first paint to kill the FOUC flash.

**Route change (`§GRAFT-13`).** `§FIX`: **no page-level `<main>` fade.** Fading the whole page on
navigation is the single most common tell of a template. Instead: the header pill, footer, week
strip, and both ledger rules persist untouched; the incoming content's hairlines replay their
`scaleX` draw at 240ms and text arrives at opacity only, **no y-translate**. Navigation should feel
like the ledger being re-ruled, not like a slide deck.

**Reduced motion (`§GRAFT-10`) — nuanced, not a kill switch.** All rules render at `scaleX(1)`
instantly. Text at opacity 1, **no translate**. Heatmap cells static. Counter shows its final value
immediately. The liveness ring does not pulse. View transitions disabled. **Retained: the 120ms
color-only feedback on hover and focus** — removing it would strip usable interaction feedback, which
`prefers-reduced-motion` does not ask for. The reading-progress line still updates, because it is
positional information rather than decoration.

**Budget.** Rule-draw, cell arrival, hovers, and underlines are all CSS. `motion` is imported only
for the counter and scroll progress. That keeps the JS story honest.

---

## 8. Per-surface

**Home** — see §4. Masthead is evilrabbit's device: bold name, gray continuation, one line, no
display heading. Lead: 14px sans, 38em. Social links as four 12px lowercase words `x · github ·
linkedin · email` with transparent 1px underlines that become `--rule-strong` on hover with zero
layout shift. **The circular icon chips on the current site are deleted** — they are its single most
generic element. `LATEST` is omitted entirely when zero posts exist (CONTEXT).

**Blog index** — header · 120 · two-line heading · rule · lead · 60 · rows grouped by year with
sticky gutter markers. Row right column: `2026-08-08 · 7 min`, tabular.

**Blog empty state** — the likely first-ship state, and one of the three display moments. `0 posts`
at `--display` in `--fg-dim`, then at `--step-3`: "Writing lands here. The first is in progress."
then `rss ↗`. No illustration, no "coming soon" badge, no fake sample essays. Rendering the absence
at monument scale converts the weakest moment on the site into one of its boldest.

**Post** — sticky header with the 1px ember progress line at its bottom edge · `← blog` 12px · title
`--step-2` (deliberately small, and more confident for it) · 12px metadata `2026-08-08 · 7 min ·
design, agents`, tabular · rule · 60 · body in Newsreader 19/1.72 at 640px, `--fg` 92%, paragraph
spacing 20px×1.5.
- `H2` is 12px mono 500 uppercase +0.1em `--fg-dim` with a hairline above spanning the measure, 60px
  above / 20px below — a heading smaller than its own body text, distinguished by weight, color,
  casing, and rule alone.
- Inline links: 1px `--rule-strong` underline at 3px offset → `--ember` on hover in 140ms.
- Blockquote: gutter-pulled (§4), no quote marks.
- Code: Geist Mono 13px on `--bg-raise`, hairline top and bottom only, full-bleed to the measure, no
  rounded corners. `sugar-high` tokens mapped to `--fg` / `--fg-muted` / `--fg-dim` / `--ember`, no
  rainbow.
- Post footer: prev/next in the row grammar at `--step-3`.
- MDX stays sanitized (`rehype-sanitize`) — the existing hardening is not to be regressed.

**Projects** — header · 120 · two-line heading, label reads `PROJECTS / 8` with the count tabular ·
rule · lead · 60 · 8 rows, index `01`–`08`, year in the right column swapping to `github.com ↗` on
hover. No thumbnails, no cards, no tag chips, no detail pages, no fake activity strips — CONTEXT
forbids them and the direction does not need them.

**Footer** — `© 2026 Dhruv Sharma` left · `x · github · linkedin · email · rss` right.
`§FIX-10` — the spec line must be **literally true at every breakpoint or it does not ship**. It
therefore prints only breakpoint-invariant facts, read from the same constants the layout consumes:
`53w × 7d · unit 20px`. A unit test asserts the rendered string matches the layout tokens. If the
field width is ever made responsive, the width claim stays out of the string.

**404** — `404` at `--display` in `--fg-dim`, then `this page is not in the ledger.` at `--step-0`,
then `← home`. Below, a 53×7 grid at full `--field` where every cell is L0 except those spelling
`404` in a 5×7 bitmap, lit in `--ember`. Static under reduced-motion, sweeps left→right otherwise.
~20 lines of code, speaks the site's own language, and is the thing people post.

**`/writings` → `/blog`** 301 and `/feed.xml` RSS both survive the rebuild unchanged.

---

## 9. Acceptance tests (screenshot- or script-verifiable)

A piece is not done until its tests pass. These are what the critic checks.

1. At 1440×900, the lifetime numeral **and** the complete year grid are fully visible without
   scrolling, and the numeral is the largest element on screen.
2. `curl -s localhost:3000` contains the real token total. No hydration mismatch in the console.
3. Every vertical gap on every page is a multiple of 20px.
4. Exactly three elements sitewide use `--display`.
5. No mono font is applied to any multi-sentence prose block.
6. `--ember` appears only in the seven enumerated places.
7. Nothing on the page animates after 2s from load (no perpetual motion) — verify by comparing two
   screenshots 5s apart; they must be pixel-identical.
8. Zero horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1056, 1280, 1440, 2560.
9. Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390.
10. The footer spec string equals the actual layout tokens.
11. Lighthouse: performance ≥95, a11y 100, best-practices 100, SEO 100. CLS = 0.
12. Full keyboard traversal of the heatmap including `PageUp`/`PageDown`, with the readout announced.
13. Both themes pass their stated contrast ratios.
14. A blind judge shown ours and dai.is-a.dev cannot describe them as the same design language.

---

## 10. Standing prohibitions

No cards. No box shadows. No border-radius above 4px except the header pill and the avatar. No
gradients except the heatmap ramp and the leader mask. No background textures. No icon chips. No
hamburger menu. No thumbnails on Projects. No project detail pages. No scroll-jacking. No parallax.
No pinned sections. No particle hero. No "coming soon" badges. No fake data. No perpetual animation.
No dashboard grammar. No page-level fade on route change. No seventh font size. No eighth ember use.

# postplan

Publish a plan, report, or artifact as a public HTML page at `https://<draft-id>.postplan.dev`.


4. **Report the URL**, adding `https://postplan.dev/d/<draft-id>/raw` when the user wants the source HTML.

A draft's URL never changes as versions accumulate, so a draft is the right shape for a progress tracker, status page, or running log — share the link once, then keep re-uploading. To keep one:

- **Keep the source file at a durable path** — `~/postplan-drafts/<name>.html`, or inside the repo the work lives in. A scratch or temp path loses the file, and a lost file means a new draft and a dead link.

#!/bin/zsh
# One blind Awwwards A/B round: shoot ours, shuffle against a reference, judge with
# gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh reasoning, then reveal the key.
#
# usage: judge.sh <name> <route> <ref.png> [fold|full] [1440x900|390x844] [dark|light]
#
# Prints the judge's verdict, then the KEY mapping, then the resolved winner.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
ROOT="$PWD"

NAME="$1"; ROUTE="$2"; REF="$3"; MODE="${4:-full}"; SIZE="${5:-1440x900}"; THEME="${6:-dark}"
W="${SIZE%x*}"; H="${SIZE#*x}"

WORK="$ROOT/.critique/rounds/$NAME"
rm -rf "$WORK"; mkdir -p "$WORK"

"$ROOT/.critique/shoot.sh" "judge-$NAME" "$WORK" ours "$ROUTE" "$W" "$H" "$MODE" "$THEME" >/dev/null
python3 "$ROOT/.critique/blind.py" "$WORK" "ours:$WORK/ours.png" "ref:$REF" >/dev/null

REFNAME="$(basename "$REF" .png)"

cat >"$WORK/prompt.md" <<PROMPT
You are judging two personal-site screenshots, attached to this message as images.
They are sample-A and sample-B in the order attached (A first, B second).
You do not know which is which and you must not try to find out. Do NOT read any file named KEY.json.
Do not browse. Judge only the two attached images.

Judge as an Awwwards jury member scoring for Site of the Day and Best UI/UX. You are a HARSH critic.
"Clean and minimal" is not a compliment and is not a reason to win. Award the win to the site that
shows more evidence of deliberate craft: a real typographic system, a considered spatial rhythm, a
memorable and specific idea, and detail that could not have come from a template.

Penalise: generic component chrome (cards, chips, pills-for-their-own-sake), dead vertical space,
misaligned optical edges, a fold with no event, decorative elements that carry no information,
default-looking type scales, and anything that reads like a dashboard or a starter theme.

Answer in EXACTLY this format and nothing else:

WINNER: A or B
MARGIN: decisive | clear | narrow
BIGGEST_GAP: one sentence naming the single largest quality gap between the loser and the winner
FIX: one sentence naming the single highest-leverage change the loser should make
NOTES: at most 5 bullets of specific visual evidence, each citing what you actually see and where
PROMPT

echo "── judging '$NAME' vs $REFNAME ($MODE $SIZE $THEME) ──"
"$ROOT/.critique/luna.sh" "$WORK" "$WORK/prompt.md" "$WORK/sample-A.png" "$WORK/sample-B.png"

echo
echo "── KEY ──"
cat "$WORK/KEY.json"
echo

import json, re, sys, pathlib
w = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
key = json.loads((w / "KEY.json").read_text())

m = re.search(r"WINNER:\s*([AB])", report)
